idiom_name: interface Updatable with Updatable[] walked in a requestAnimationFrame callback
implementation_notes: The hook is an interface - TypeScript's structural typing means any object with a matching update(dt: number) method satisfies it without declaring implements - and the collection is a typed array walked in the same requestAnimationFrame callback JavaScript uses. What replaces the classic structure: the interface replaces the abstract base class and the typed array plus for...of replaces the entity manager; the types exist only to guarantee that every element of the collection can be stepped, because they are erased at runtime and the per-frame cost is identical to JavaScript. A class hierarchy is only worth it when entities share implementation (a pooled base with position and velocity), which is the part engine libraries package.
pitfalls: Structural typing accepts any object whose method name and shape match: an unrelated update() with a compatible signature silently satisfies a loosely named interface, so keep entity interfaces narrow and distinct.
Timestamps can be missing or NaN at runtime (types are erased): guard with Number.isFinite and clamp spikes before they reach every entity.
Array.splice during the walk shifts indices and skips the next entity, and push lets an entity act in the frame that created it: mark dead and filter after the loop.
Mixing plain objects and class instances in one array is allowed by the interface but splits where shared behaviour lives; decide consciously and keep one convention.
